substances.name: Water
substances.note: Expands as it freezes, so ice floats and its melting point falls under pressure.

substances.name: Carbon dioxide
substances.note: Never liquid at Earth's surface pressure: dry ice turns straight to gas.

substances.name: Methane
substances.note: Liquid in the cold of the outer system: the seas and rain of a Titan.

substances.name: Ammonia
substances.note: Mixed with water it stays liquid far below water's freezing point: oceans under ice.

substances.name: Nitrogen
substances.note: Most of Earth's air; glaciers on the coldest worlds.

substances.name: Oxygen
substances.note: Made by life; what fire and lungs need.

substances.name: Hydrogen
substances.note: The lightest fuel; most of a giant planet.

substances.name: Sulfur dioxide
substances.note: Breathed out by volcanoes; with water it makes acid clouds.

substances.name: Sulfuric acid
substances.note: The clouds of a hothouse world. (Its triple and critical points are estimates.)

substances.name: Iron
substances.note: The core of rocky worlds; the metal of an age.

substances.name: Copper
substances.note: Soft, conducts heat and current; with tin, bronze.

substances.name: Tin
substances.note: Melts in a campfire; hardens copper into bronze.

substances.name: Gold
substances.note: Doesn't tarnish; washes down rivers from its veins.

substances.name: Aluminium
substances.note: Common in rock but locked in oxides: it takes electricity to free.

substances.name: Lead
substances.note: Dense and soft; shields against radiation.

substances.name: Mercury
substances.note: The metal that's liquid at room temperature.

substances.name: Silicon
substances.note: Denser as a liquid, like water. Purified, the heart of electronics.

substances.name: Carbon (graphite)
substances.note: Never melts at ordinary pressure: it turns straight to vapour near 3900 K.

substances.name: Salt
substances.note: Left behind where seas dry up.

substances.name: Silica (quartz)
substances.note: Sand and most rock; melted, glass. (Drawn as one SiO₄ tetrahedron of its network.)

substances.name: Carbon monoxide
substances.note: What a fire starved of air makes; what pulls oxygen out of ore in a furnace. Poisonous.

substances.name: Hematite
substances.note: Red iron ore, and rust. Smelted with carbon monoxide it gives up its iron.

substances.name: Malachite
substances.note: Green copper ore. Heated, it breaks down into copper oxide, giving off CO₂ and steam (well before it could melt).

substances.name: Copper oxide
substances.note: Black copper oxide: one step from metal, given carbon monoxide and heat.

substances.name: Calcite (limestone)
substances.note: Limestone and chalk, laid down in seas. Burned in a kiln it gives quicklime and CO₂ (well before it could melt).

substances.name: Quicklime
substances.note: Burned limestone: the base of mortar, cement and concrete.

substances.name: Glucose
substances.note: Sugar: what light builds from CO₂ and water, and what living things burn. (It chars before it could boil; drawn as its ring.)

substances.name: Olivine
substances.note: Green mineral of the mantle and of basalt. The first to crystallise from cooling magma.

substances.name: Pyroxene
substances.note: Dark chains of silica: much of basalt and the mantle.

substances.name: Feldspar
substances.note: The commonest mineral of the crust: the pink and white grains of granite. Weathers into clay.

substances.name: Plagioclase
substances.note: Sodium feldspar: the pale crystals in basalt and andesite.

substances.name: Mica
substances.note: Splits into thin glittering sheets. (It breaks down before it could melt.)

substances.name: Kaolinite (clay)
substances.note: Clay: weathered feldspar. Wet, it shapes; fired in a kiln, it gives up its water and becomes pottery.

substances.name: Fired clay
substances.note: Clay that has been through the kiln: hard, and water won't soften it again. Pottery and brick.

substances.name: Magnetite
substances.note: Black iron ore, and a natural magnet: lodestone. Smelts like hematite.

substances.name: Chalcopyrite
substances.note: Brassy copper ore from hydrothermal veins. Roasted, it gives off sulfur dioxide and leaves copper and iron oxides.

substances.name: Cassiterite
substances.note: Tin ore: heavy, so it gathers in river gravels below the granite it weathered from.

substances.name: Galena
substances.note: Lead ore: silvery grey cubes. Often carries silver.

substances.name: Lead oxide
substances.note: Roasted galena: one step from lead.

substances.name: Pyrite
substances.note: Fool's gold. Roasted it gives sulfur dioxide; it sparks against steel. (It breaks down long before it could melt.)

substances.name: Sulfur
substances.note: Yellow crystals around volcanic vents. Burns with a blue flame into sulfur dioxide.

substances.name: Bronze
substances.note: Copper with about a tenth tin: harder than either, and it melts lower than copper, so it casts well. The first great alloy.

substances.name: Cast iron
substances.note: Iron that has soaked up carbon in the furnace: it melts hundreds of degrees lower than pure iron and pours into moulds, but it's brittle.

substances.name: Steel
substances.note: Iron with a little carbon: hard and tough. Made by burning most of the carbon out of molten cast iron.

substances.name: Pewter
substances.note: Tin hardened with a little lead: plates, cups and toys. Melts in a cooking fire.

substances.name: Zinc
substances.note: With copper, brass. It boils not far above where it melts, so it's hard to smelt.

substances.name: Wood
substances.note: Cellulose, as far as chemistry cares: burns in air; heated without enough air it chars to charcoal. (It chars long before it could melt.) It never melts: it chars or burns long before (its melting and boiling points are placeholders far above any fire).

substances.name: Soda ash
substances.note: From burned seaweed or dried salt lakes. Melted with sand it makes glass at a heat a fire can reach.

substances.name: Glass
substances.note: Sand and soda melted together and cooled before it can crystallise: clear, and it keeps the weather out.

substances.name: Slaked lime
substances.note: Quicklime that has drunk water, hissing hot. Mixed with sand it's mortar, which slowly turns back to limestone in the air.

substances.name: Rubber
substances.note: Natural rubber (polyisoprene), from tree sap: soft, springy and grippy, a tyre's tread. It burns and breaks down long before it could melt (its melting and boiling points are placeholders far above any fire).

substances.name: Sodium
substances.note: Soft, silvery and furious with water: it tears hydrogen out of it, hot enough to light it.

substances.name: Potassium
substances.note: Sodium's wilder cousin: on water it lights its own hydrogen with a lilac flame.

substances.name: Magnesium
substances.note: A light metal that burns blinding white once it's hot enough.

substances.name: Cobalt
substances.note: A hard metal; its oxide turns glass deep blue.

substances.name: Chlorine
substances.note: A yellow-green choking gas.

substances.name: Hydrogen chloride
substances.note: Dissolved in water, it's hydrochloric acid: it eats metals and gives off hydrogen.

substances.name: Nitric acid
substances.note: A fuming acid; it makes nitrates, the oxygen in gunpowder.

substances.name: Nitrogen dioxide
substances.note: The brown fumes off nitric acid at work.

substances.name: Caustic soda
substances.note: A strong base: it neutralises acids and eats grease and aluminium.

substances.name: Caustic potash
substances.note: Lye from wood ash: a strong base.

substances.name: Alumina
substances.note: Aluminium's oxide: corundum, sapphire, and thermite's ash.

substances.name: Aluminium chloride
substances.note: What aluminium becomes in hydrochloric acid.

substances.name: Iron chloride
substances.note: What iron becomes in hydrochloric acid: a green solution.

substances.name: Zinc chloride
substances.note: What zinc becomes in hydrochloric acid; a soldering flux.

substances.name: Zinc oxide
substances.note: White zinc ash; zinc burns to it with a blue-green flame.

substances.name: Magnesia
substances.note: Magnesium's white ash; a furnace lining that won't melt.

substances.name: Cobalt oxide
substances.note: A pinch makes glass cobalt blue.

substances.name: Manganese oxide
substances.note: Pyrolusite: glassmakers' soap (it clears iron's green) and, more of it, purple.

substances.name: Saltpetre
substances.note: Gives up its oxygen when hot: with charcoal and sulfur it's gunpowder.

substances.name: Potash
substances.note: Wood ash leached and dried: a flux for glass, and gunpowder's ash.

substances.name: Potassium sulfide
substances.note: Part of gunpowder's smoke.

substances.name: Sodium sulfate
substances.note: The salt left when caustic soda meets sulfuric acid.

substances.name: Propane
substances.note: Bottled gas: a blowtorch's fuel, about 2000 °C burning in air.

substances.name: Ethanol
substances.note: Alcohol: a fuel that burns with a clean blue flame.

substances.name: Octane
substances.note: The heart of petrol: a lot of energy in a little liquid.
